units.function: Generated package-level release ledger for paperclipai versions 0.2.1 through 0.3.1, primarily recording lockstep workspace dependency version updates and generic version-bump/stable-release preparation notes.
units.dependencyDirection: Release documentation -> published CLI and workspace package versions. It names adapter/db/shared/server package coordinates but defines no runtime dependency or compatibility contract and contains no links to migration guides, issues, pull requests for most entries, or signed release artifacts.
units.keyDataModels: Semantic package versions and dependency version lists. There is no schema/API/event/adapter compatibility matrix, deprecation state, migration ID, security advisory, release channel, support window, artifact digest or rollback boundary.
units.lifecycle: Chronological entries show 0.2.1-0.2.7 patch bumps followed by 0.3.0 minor and 0.3.1 patch, with workspace packages generally bumped together. The document does not describe installation-to-installation state transitions, database migration order, downgrade behavior, data backup requirements or release support lifecycle.
units.testAssessment: Documentation has no executable validation. Package and release tests elsewhere cannot prove this changelog is complete or behaviorally meaningful. The single-file history attributes all 138 current lines to one commit, so per-release authorship and contemporaneous traceability are absent from this artifact.
units.designRationale: Automated changeset-style dependency lists make lockstep monorepo publishing visible and reduce manual version drift. Generic generated notes are adequate as a package registry accompaniment but not as an operator or adopter upgrade contract.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a reliable release train for managed-cloud and self-hosted customers, including API/event/Connector/schema compatibility, security fixes, migration and rollback instructions, support windows and provenance for every release.
units.companyOsFit: Retain automated package-version generation only as supplementary metadata. Company OS must own a human-reviewed release manifest and upgrade contract with exact commit/tag/digests, database migration range, API/event/SDK compatibility, deprecations, security impact, backup/rollback steps, deployment-profile notes and explicit no-downgrade boundaries. Competitive monitoring should use Paperclip commits/releases directly, not this changelog alone.
units.responsibilityConflict: No direct responsibility-domain implementation exists. Operationally, opaque release notes prevent an accountable human from understanding which authority, data or evidence semantics change during upgrade; such changes must be explicit approval inputs for enterprise deployment.
evidence: Document covers package versions 0.2.1 through 0.3.1 and mostly says Version bump, Stable release preparation and Updated dependencies
git history/blame: all current lines attribute to 73eb23734f25c570d88665e672f80d740797c632 (2026-04-20, docs: use structured agent mentions in paperclip skill (#4103))
Visible package evolution includes @paperclipai/adapter-openclaw in 0.2.x, adapter-openclaw-gateway by 0.3.x, and additional cursor/gemini/opencode/pi adapters without behavioral migration notes
units.securityFindings: No security advisories, vulnerability identifiers, credential/schema impact, artifact signatures/digests, supply-chain provenance or urgent-upgrade guidance are present. Generic dependency bumps make it impossible to determine whether a release contains a security fix or trust-boundary change. The changelog must not be used as sole evidence for safe adoption or upgrade.
